question: Har Ghar Tiranga campaign was launched for which of the following national day celebrations?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Independence Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Har Ghar Tiranga" campaign was an initiative of the Government of India to encourage citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes.
 
• This campaign was launched as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, marking 75 years of India's independence.
 
• The campaign aimed to deepen the connection of citizens with the national flag and instill a sense of patriotism.
 
• It was officially launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and was observed from August 13 to 15, 2022.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independence Day**

 
 
• India celebrates its Independence Day on August 15th every year.
 
• This day marks the end of British rule in 1947 and the establishment of a free and independent Indian nation.
 
• The day is marked with flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, and cultural events across the country.
 
• The Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the Red Fort in New Delhi and delivers an address to the nation.
 
 
 
• **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav**
 
 
• Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an initiative by the Government of India to celebrate and commemorate 75 years of progressive India and the glorious history of its people, culture, and achievements.
 
• The Mahotsav is dedicated to the people of India who have been instrumental in bringing India thus far in its evolutionary journey.
 
• The official journey of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav commenced on 12th March 2021 which started a 75-week countdown to our 75th anniversary of independence and will end post a year on 15th August 2023.
 
• It aims to celebrate the spirit of independence and the sense of duty towards the nation.
 
 
 
• **National Flag of India**
 
 
• The national flag of India is a horizontal tricolor of deep saffron (Kesari) at the top, white in the middle, and dark green at the bottom in equal proportion.
 
• In the center of the white band is a navy blue wheel which represents the chakra.
 
• This wheel is a representation of the Ashoka Chakra at Sarnath, and it has 24 spokes.
 
• The flag was adopted in its present form during a meeting of the Constituent Assembly held on 22 July 1947, a few days before India's independence from the British on 15 August 1947.
